generations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production game sprite animation sheet for original hero CH03 industrial signal technician. Create a NEW 1536x1024 transparent PNG containing EXACTLY SIX full-body poses in a clean three-column, two-row grid. Reading order is left to right, first top row then bottom row. There are NO drawn grid lines, labels, titles or numbers.
Reference images are identity, anatomy, costume, weapon and painted rendering references. Preserve this exact original man: adult medium build, wavy short black hair, mustache and small beard, warm skin, teal scarf and shoulder fabric, ivory-white jacket/armor with bronze edging and fasteners, brown armored trousers and industrial boots, dark fingerless gloves. Preserve the unmistakable large circular brass signal dish attached to his upper back, three ivory/bronze cylindrical antenna coils beside it, small cyan crystal canister at belt, all cables and straps. Preserve the same short-handled brass bifurcated needle projector with cyan crystal between its fork prongs, continuously held in his weapon hand. Never replace it with a gun, spear, staff, wrench or sword. The free hand operates the existing cyan chest/core controller, not an added floating object.
Rendering must closely match the references' highly finished hand-painted fantasy-industrial character concept art: crisp painterly edges, believable materials, nuanced folds, detailed brass and leather, soft coherent upper-left lighting, anatomically credible limbs, visible separated fingers where scale allows. Same anatomical body size and head size in all six poses, same camera, no zoom between frames. Character should occupy about 385 pixels in anatomical standing height in each 512x512 cell, with substantial transparent padding and complete silhouette including every hand, foot, dish, coil, cable and weapon. Each pose strictly confined within its own cell and must not overlap any other. Keep the two boot contact points on a consistent local floor baseline, around y=455 in each cell. Weight-bearing feet and knees must read as physically supporting his body, no levitation, no skating, no mirrored hands, no extra digits.
Animation meaning: this is the F skill, a bodily CORE COMMAND causing already-deployed remote nodes to detonate simultaneously. The nodes and blasts are NOT drawn. This is not shooting. The needle projector stays tucked close or hangs safely low throughout; its weapon arm must never extend outward to aim/fire. Hand, elbow, shoulder, ribcage and knees articulate with clear purposeful pose differences, not simple translated duplicates.
Six consecutive poses:
1 gather: projector held near his weapon-side hip pointing diagonally down, empty hand comes close to chest cyan core, modest knees bend, shoulders gather.
2 tune: free gloved hand grips and twists the chest core controller, elbow lifted a little, weight coils over supported legs; weapon stays tucked at side.
3 command: the single committed command beat: shoulder drives downward as the free hand presses the core controller DOWN against his own chest/upper abdomen, broader firm stance, strong believable bracing, no outstretched shooting arm; held projector remains low alongside thigh.
4 contract: command recoil is absorbed through bent elbows and a compact ribcage, torso slightly folds back into center, knees support; weapon elbow draws inward.
5 release_core: free hand releases the core and separates a short distance from his own chest, chest begins opening on a breath, knees soften, projector still low.
6 ready: settled balanced low ready, weapon near hip pointing down, free hand relaxed beside torso, stance visually returns to reference idle.
Transparent background must be true alpha transparency. No ground, backdrop, checkerboard printed into image, cast shadow, glow halos outside the character, fire, explosion, smoke, magic rings, UI, text or watermarks. The cyan core can be visibly luminous within its metal housing only.
View for ALL six poses: exact FRONT three-quarter overhead isometric view from reference image 1, front/chest and face visible, character facing lower right of image (southeast). Maintain the identical front camera and silhouette orientation for every frame. Image 2 is only supporting back-equipment consistency.
